description: Replace the separate NearMeTopic type with GuideTopicSlug so both guide and near-me features share one topic vocabulary
steps: In lib/near-me.ts, delete the NEAR_ME_TOPICS constant and NearMeTopic type
Import GuideTopicSlug from content/guides.ts and re-export it as NearMeTopic: export type NearMeTopic = GuideTopicSlug

Update every TOPIC_META key from the old slugs to the guide slugs: 'setup' → 'home-admin', 'survive' → 'food-eating', 'get-around' → 'getting-around', 'health' → 'health-wellbeing', 'connect' → 'social-belonging'
Update the label field in each TOPIC_META entry to match the guide topic name exactly: 'Food & Eating', 'Getting Around', 'Health & Wellbeing', 'Home & Admin', 'Social & Belonging'
Update parseTopic() default return value from 'survive' to 'food-eating' and ensure it validates against GuideTopicSlug values
Delete LEGACY_CATEGORY_TO_TOPIC from content/guides.ts — it is now redundant
Verify no TypeScript errors across the codebase after the rename
Verify the Near Me page still loads correctly with the unified type

description: Update TOPIC_COLORS in near-me-map.tsx and all topic conditional logic in near-me-view.tsx to use guide slugs
steps: In components/near-me/near-me-map.tsx, update TOPIC_COLORS keys from old slugs to guide slugs: 'food-eating' → '#e07b39', 'getting-around' → '#3a6aaa', 'health-wellbeing' → '#3a8a5a', 'home-admin' → '#2a8a7a', 'social-belonging' → '#7a6aaa'

In near-me-view.tsx, find every instance of topic === 'survive' and replace with topic === 'food-eating'; same for 'health' → 'health-wellbeing', 'connect' → 'social-belonging', 'setup' → 'home-admin', 'get-around' → 'getting-around'
Update the enabledTopics set from ['survive'] to all five guide slugs: ['food-eating', 'getting-around', 'health-wellbeing', 'home-admin', 'social-belonging']

Update subtypes in TOPIC_META: social-belonging subtypes rename to { slug: 'community-spaces', label: 'Parks & free' } and { slug: 'social-venues', label: 'Bars & social' }; getting-around subtypes rename to { slug: 'public-transit', label: 'Trains & trams' } and { slug: 'cycling', label: 'Bikes & walking' }

Update any ?topic= URL params generated internally to use guide slugs (check LandingHubSidebar saved-place links and guide nearMeDeeplink values — guide deeplinks already use guide slugs so they will now work correctly without the legacy fallback)
Verify topic tab switching works correctly for all 5 tabs after the rename
Verify the map marker color for each topic is unchanged visually — only the key names changed, not the hex values

description: Thread topic and subtype parameters from fetchPlaces() through the Next.js route to the Python backend
steps: In near-me-view.tsx fetchPlaces() (approx. lines 300–360), append &topic={activeTopic} to the fetch URL always, and &subtype={activeSubtype} only when activeSubtype is not 'all'

In app/api/nearby-interest/route.ts, read topic and subtype from searchParams alongside suburb; validate topic against GuideTopicSlug values (reject unknown values with 400); pass both to fetchNearbyInterest()
In lib/near-me-api.ts, extend fetchNearbyInterest() to accept topic?: string and subtype?: string and add them to the URLSearchParams sent upstream when non-null
Verify /api/nearby-interest?suburb=Richmond&topic=health-wellbeing&subtype=gp-clinics returns clinic results, not restaurant results
Verify switching topic tabs triggers a new fetch with the updated topic param
Verify switching subtype chips triggers a new fetch with the updated subtype param

description: [BACKEND FIX REQUIRED] Python server must map topic and subtype to appropriate SerpAPI query strings
steps: In the Python backend /api/nearby-interest handler, read topic and subtype query params
Define a QUERY_MAP dict mapping (topic, subtype) tuples to SerpAPI 'q' strings using the guide slugs:
('food-eating', 'food-dining')        → 'cheap restaurants cafes food'
('food-eating', 'groceries')          → 'supermarkets grocery stores'
('getting-around', 'public-transit')  → 'train station tram stop'
('getting-around', 'cycling')         → 'bus stop bicycle hire station'
('health-wellbeing', 'gp-clinics')    → 'GP medical centre bulk billing clinic'
('health-wellbeing', 'mental-health') → 'psychologist counsellor mental health service'
('home-admin', 'services')            → 'government services community centre settlement support'
('home-admin', 'libraries')           → 'public library'
('social-belonging', 'community-spaces') → 'park community centre multicultural centre free'
('social-belonging', 'social-venues')    → 'bar pub social club'
When subtype is absent or 'all', use a broader per-topic query covering all subtypes
Fall back to the food-eating/food-dining query when both topic and subtype are absent
Verify each (topic, subtype) combination returns meaningfully different SerpAPI result sets

description: Add an 'All' first-position subtype chip per topic so users can browse unfiltered results
steps: In lib/near-me.ts, prepend { slug: 'all', label: 'All' } as the first entry in every topic's subtypes array
In near-me-view.tsx, initialise activeSubtype to 'all' when a topic is first selected or the page loads
Omit the subtype param from the fetch URL when activeSubtype === 'all'
Render the 'All' chip with the same pill style as other subtype chips; highlight it when selected
Selecting a specific subtype deselects 'All'; selecting 'All' deselects the active subtype
Switching topics resets activeSubtype to 'all'
Verify all 5 topic tabs show the 'All' chip as the first option in the subtype row

description: food-eating (formerly survive) tab renders correctly with updated slug and continues to use CardGridList
steps: Confirm topic === 'food-eating' still resolves to layout === 'card-grid' after the slug rename
Verify service options chips (dine-in, takeaway, delivery) still render on food-eating cards — the existing condition was topic === 'survive', update it to topic === 'food-eating'
Verify price tags ('$', '$$', '$$$') still render as tag chips on food-eating cards
Verify the map heading reads 'Cheap eats & groceries near {suburb}' on the food-eating tab
Verify orange map markers (#e07b39) appear on the food-eating tab

description: getting-around tab opens with CompactList and shows transit mode badges inferred from the place type field
steps: Confirm topic === 'getting-around' resolves to layout === 'map-focus' and renders CompactList
In CompactList, define a TRANSIT_BADGE lookup: 'train' → '🚂 Train', 'tram' → '🚊 Tram', 'bus' → '🚌 Bus', 'bicycle' or 'bike' → '🚲 Bike'
Match place.type (case-insensitive substring) against the lookup keys; render the first matching badge as a small rounded pill using text-[11px] bg-blue-100 text-blue-700 px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full
When no type matches, render a generic '🗺 Transit' badge with the same styling
Suppress the Call button for all getting-around places — transit stops have no bookable phone line

Replace the Google Maps Directions anchor with a 'Plan journey' link to https://www.ptv.vic.gov.au/journey (new tab, rel=noreferrer) for the public-transit subtype; keep Directions for the cycling subtype
Verify blue map markers (#3a6aaa) appear on the getting-around tab
Verify Train / Tram / Bus / Bike badges render on rows with matching type values

description: health-wellbeing tab opens with DetailList and preserves all health-specific UX: crisis banner, bulk-billing nudge, open-status emphasis
steps: Confirm topic === 'health-wellbeing' resolves to layout === 'list-focus' and renders DetailList
Update the bulk-billing synthetic tag injection condition from topic === 'health' to topic === 'health-wellbeing'
Update the CrisisLineBanner render condition from topic === 'health' to topic === 'health-wellbeing'
Update the rating-suppression condition in the map popup card from topic === 'connect' to topic === 'social-belonging' (see social-belonging item) and verify health-wellbeing still shows ratings
In DetailList for topic === 'health-wellbeing', render the open/closed badge as the first element below the place name; style open as bg-green-100 text-green-700 and closed as bg-red-100 text-red-700
When activeSubtype === 'mental-health', display heading 'Mental health services near {suburb}' instead of the default 'Clinics & GPs near {suburb}'
Ensure CrisisLineBanner remains visible even when places.length === 0 on the health-wellbeing tab
Verify green map markers (#3a8a5a) appear on the health-wellbeing tab

description: home-admin tab opens with DetailList and renders government services and libraries with appropriate actions
steps: Confirm topic === 'home-admin' resolves to layout === 'list-focus' and renders DetailList
In DetailList for topic === 'home-admin', render the 'Visit website' button prominently — government services typically have websites but not always a direct call line
Suppress the Call button for home-admin places where place.phone is absent rather than rendering an empty tel: link
Do NOT inject the 'Bulk-billing: call to confirm' tag for home-admin — this nudge is health-wellbeing only
Verify the heading 'Services & support near {suburb}' renders correctly above the DetailList
Verify switching between 'Services & info' and 'Libraries' subtype chips triggers a new fetch and returns distinct place categories
Verify teal map markers (#2a8a7a) appear on the home-admin tab

description: social-belonging tab opens with CompactList and suppresses ratings; adds contextual nudges per subtype
steps: Confirm topic === 'social-belonging' resolves to layout === 'map-focus' and renders CompactList
Update the rating-suppression condition from topic === 'connect' to topic === 'social-belonging' in CompactList and in the map popup card

For topic === 'social-belonging' and subtype === 'community-spaces', render a small informational chip on each row: '📅 Check for events' styled as bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 border border-amber-200 text-[10px] rounded-full px-2 py-0.5

For topic === 'social-belonging' and subtype === 'social-venues', render price tag chips from place.tags ('$', '$$', '$$$') to the right of the place name as bg-minuri-teal/10 text-minuri-teal rounded px-1.5 text-[11px]
Verify purple map markers (#7a6aaa) appear on the social-belonging tab
Verify no rating badge renders on any social-belonging place card
Verify the event nudge chip appears only on community-spaces subtype rows

description: Replace synthetic distance estimate with real Haversine distance calculated from user GPS coordinates
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, find the distanceKm assignment inside fetchPlaces() (approx. line 347): distanceKm: 0.4 + index * 0.7
Add a haversineKm(lat1: number, lng1: number, lat2: number, lng2: number): number helper in lib/near-me.ts using the spherical law of cosines (R = 6371 km)
When userCoords is non-null, compute distanceKm = haversineKm(userCoords.lat, userCoords.lng, place.lat, place.lng) for each mapped place
When userCoords is null, set distanceKm to undefined so no distance label renders on any card
After mapping, when usingLocation === true, sort places ascending by distanceKm before calling setPlaces()
Verify that with location enabled, the closest place appears first in the list
Verify that without location, no distance label renders on any place row

description: Topic-aware empty state shows actionable suburb suggestions matched to the topic context
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, when places.length === 0 and status === 'success', render a supplementary suggestion line below the emptyPrompt

Define EMPTY_SUGGESTIONS per guide topic slug: 'home-admin' → 'Try Dandenong or Footscray — both have large settlement support hubs', 'getting-around' → 'Try the CBD or inner suburbs for the best transit coverage', 'health-wellbeing' → 'Try a neighbouring suburb, or use the crisis line numbers above to find support now', 'social-belonging' → 'Try Fitzroy, Footscray, or Sunshine for active multicultural community spaces', 'food-eating' → keep existing emptyPrompt only
Style the suggestion as text-muted-foreground text-sm italic mt-1 — not an error state
Verify each topic shows its correct suggestion when a search returns zero results
Verify food-eating shows no additional suggestion line

Verify clicking the Bridge CTA on a food-eating guide (e.g. cheap-eats-when-broke, nearMeDeeplink contains ?topic=food-eating) opens Near Me with the food-eating tab pre-selected
